newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber slow, Thais mull RSS3 offers.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber slow, Thais mull RSS3 offers.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market floundered around on Monday with most of the trade keeping an eye on talks between the Thai government and sellers for 7,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber, traders said on Monday.

"I guess the trade did not go through. They're haggling about the price," a dealer for a North American rubber brokerage house said, adding Bangkok was sticking to its price of 123.50 U.S. cents a kg against seller prices of at least 124.00 cents.
"It's not really clear what's going to happen to the proposed deal. We're waiting for more word about it," a trader for a commodity house in Singapore said.
Action in the local market was also slow with prices holding steady in dull trading. One dealer predicted conditions may not improve ahead of the Easter holidays this week.
"It's a pre-holiday market already," the trader said. "Nobody has bid me anything through the day."
"Physical demand was really slow today. We're not getting much in terms of inquiries," another dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen unchanged at 121.00 U.S. cents a kg. October/December RSS1 was seen steady at 180.00 Singapore cents (US$1.26) a kg.
